decisions.choice: the fifth vision: a gold lampstand fed by two olive trees, with a word for Zerubbabel
decisions.reason: Zechariah sees a lampstand of gold with seven lamps, kept supplied with oil from two olive trees beside it (verses 2-3, 11-12). In the middle of the vision comes a word for Zerubbabel the governor: the temple will be finished not by human strength but by the LORD's Spirit (verses 6-10). The angel explains the seven lamps as the eyes of the LORD (verse 10) and the two trees as two anointed ones who stand beside the Lord of all the earth (verse 14).

decisions.choice: like someone roused from sleep: Zechariah is stirred to full attention
decisions.reason: The prophet is not said to have fallen asleep, but he was in a state like sleep, and the angel rouses him to see the next vision, as Daniel was roused in his visions (Daniel 8:18; 10:9-10). The angel "came back", as if he had stepped away after the last vision.

decisions.choice: a person / a man; their / his (L); someone (B, R)
decisions.reason: The comparison is with anyone woken from sleep, so Literal gives "a man ... his" the gender setting, and Balanced and Readable say "someone".

decisions.choice: {{gender:une personne|un homme}} (L), with "son sommeil" and no span on the possessive
decisions.reason: The Hebrew *ish* here means anyone; French Literal puts the setting on the noun, as the English, and "son" agrees with "sommeil", so it needs none.

decisions.choice: "un hombre ... su sueño", with no gender span
decisions.reason: Spanish "su" covers both sexes, and "un hombre" here is the comparison of the Hebrew ('ish) for anyone; B and R say "alguien", which needs no span.

decisions.choice: "mtu ... usingizini mwake" with no gender span
decisions.reason: "Mtu" and "mwake" cover everyone, so the English gender span has no Swahili counterpart.

decisions.choice: "một người ... giấc ngủ", with no gender span
decisions.reason: Vietnamese "người" covers both and needs no possessive with "giấc ngủ"; the English gender spans have no counterpart.

decisions.choice: "like a man roused from his sleep" is "잠에서 깨어나는 사람처럼", with no gender span
decisions.reason: Korean "사람" is not marked for sex and needs no pronoun, so the English Literal's gender spans have no Korean counterpart.

decisions.choice: and I said: the form the Hebrew text tells the reader to read
decisions.reason: The written letters of the Hebrew text have "and he said", and the form marked to be read aloud has "and I said". The reading form fits the dialogue: the angel asks, and Zechariah answers.

decisions.choice: a lampstand of gold with a bowl on top: a lampstand fed from an oil bowl above its lamps
decisions.reason: The word is the one used for the seven-branched lampstand of the tabernacle (Exodus 25:31-40), which the priests kept supplied with oil (Exodus 27:20-21). This one is different: a bowl on top holds the oil and feeds the lamps, and the oil comes from two living olive trees (verse 3, 12), not from human hands. The word for bowl is used of a basin or a bowl-shaped lamp (Ecclesiastes 12:6).

decisions.choice: seven and seven spouts: seven spouts on each of the seven lamps
alternatives: seven pipes, one to each lamp
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "seven and seven", a way of saying "seven each". The word translated "spouts" is found only here; it seems to come from a verb for pouring, and may mean the pinched lips of a clay lamp where a wick lay, or pipes carrying oil from the bowl. Clay lamps with seven spouts around the rim have been found in the land of Israel. If so, the lampstand had seven lamps, each with seven flames. Others read seven pipes in all, one to each lamp.

decisions.choice: look (L); spouts (L, B); places for wicks (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew order and "look". Balanced and Readable say "each of the lamps has seven", which is what "seven and seven" means (m3), and Readable says what a spout is for. Zechariah's description runs on into verse 3, where the quotation mark closes.

decisions.choice: "un chandelier tout en or", "une vasque", "becs" (L, B)
decisions.reason: The term sheet's words for the vision, so that Revelation 11:4's "chandeliers" and "oliviers" can be recognized; Zechariah's answer runs on in « » to the end of verse 3.

decisions.choice: "un candelabro todo de oro" (L, B), "de oro macizo" (R); "depósito" for the bowl
decisions.reason: The term sheet's words for the lampstand, as 1 Chronicles 28:15 in Spanish. Zechariah's answer runs into verse 3 and is closed there.

decisions.choice: "kinara cha taa cha dhahabu tupu"; "mirija" (L, B), "sehemu za kuwekea utambi" (R)
decisions.reason: The lampstand is worded as the term sheet sets and as Exodus 25:31. The spouts are "mirija" at L and B; Readable describes the places for wicks, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "chân đèn" for the lampstand, "bằng vàng ròng" at R
decisions.reason: The terms note, as Exodus 25:31; the bowl is "cái bầu", the oil reservoir the meaning decision describes.

decisions.choice: "a lampstand all of gold" is "온통 금으로 된 등잔대" (L) and "순금 등잔대" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The term sheet's word (Exodus 25:31); these are oil lamps, not candles. Zechariah's answer is in 합쇼체 to the angel.

decisions.choice: a word for Zerubbabel inside the vision
alternatives: a passage moved here from elsewhere
decisions.reason: Instead of explaining the lampstand at once, the angel gives a word for Zerubbabel, which runs to the middle of verse 10; then the explanation resumes. Some think these verses once stood elsewhere, but as the text stands the word explains the vision: as the lamps burn with oil that no human hand supplies, the temple will be finished by the LORD's Spirit, not by human strength.

decisions.choice: Zerubbabel: governor of Judah and heir of David's line
decisions.reason: Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel was governor of Judah under the Persians (Haggai 1:1) and led the first group of exiles home with Joshua (Ezra 2:2; 3:2). He was a grandson of King Jehoiachin (1 Chronicles 3:17-19), so he was of the royal family of David. Haggai calls him the LORD's chosen signet ring (Haggai 2:23). With Joshua he led the rebuilding of the temple.

decisions.choice: might ... power: any human strength, whether armies, wealth or effort
decisions.reason: The first word means strength or ability, and is used for armies and for wealth (Exodus 14:4; Deuteronomy 8:17-18). The second means strength or power in general. Together they rule out every human resource as the means by which the work will be done.

decisions.choice: by my Spirit: by the LORD's own power at work
decisions.reason: The word means wind, breath or spirit, and here it is the LORD's Spirit: his power at work among his people. Haggai 2:5 had promised, "My Spirit remains among you; do not fear." Like the oil that flows to the lamps from the living trees, the Spirit supplies what the builders cannot.

decisions.choice: Not by might, nor by power, but by my Spirit, at every level
decisions.reason: The saying keeps one wording at every level, as set for this verse, because readers know it and quote it. "Spirit" is capitalized for God's Spirit, as in Isaiah. The angel's words are in double quotation marks, and the word to Zerubbabel is in single marks inside them; both close at the end of verse 7.

decisions.choice: "Ni par la puissance, ni par la force, mais par mon Esprit" at every level
alternatives: "Ce n'est ni par la puissance ni par la force"
decisions.reason: The English keeps one wording at every level for this well-known line; French does the same, with "Esprit" capitalised for God's Spirit, as the term sheet.

decisions.choice: "No por poderío ni por fuerza, sino por mi Espíritu"
decisions.reason: The line is drafted from the Hebrew (hayil, koah, ruah) and kept close at every level, as the English is; it avoids the familiar wordings "No con ejército, ni con fuerza" and "No será por la fuerza ni por ningún poder". God's Spirit is capitalized.

decisions.choice: « » for the angel, “ ” for the LORD's word, closed in verse 7
decisions.reason: The LORD's word to Zerubbabel is quoted inside the angel's answer and runs through verse 7.

decisions.choice: "Si kwa nguvu za jeshi, wala si kwa uwezo, bali kwa Roho wangu" at every level
decisions.reason: Chayil is strength in arms or wealth, so "nguvu za jeshi" names it, with "uwezo" for koach; drafted from the Hebrew and kept apart from the familiar Union Version line. "Roho" with a capital is God's Spirit, as the term sheet sets.

decisions.choice: "Không phải bởi năng lực, cũng không phải bởi sức mạnh, nhưng bởi Thần Linh của Ta" at every level
decisions.reason: The English keeps one wording at every level; so does the Vietnamese, with "Thần Linh" for God's Spirit as the terms note gives. Drafted from the Hebrew, not from the 1926 "quyền thế ... năng lực ... Thần ta".

decisions.choice: "Not by might, nor by power, but by my Spirit" is "힘으로도 아니고 능력(B 권세)으로도 아니며, 오직 나의 영으로 된다", drafted from the gloss; God's Spirit is "영"
alternatives: "힘으로 되지 아니하며 능력으로 되지 아니하고 오직 나의 영으로 되느니라"
decisions.reason: The term sheet asks for this line to be drafted from the gloss and for the older wording with -느니라 not to be reused; Readable says what kind of might and power is meant ("군대의 힘", "사람의 능력"), as the meaning decision does. "성령" stays for the New Testament.

decisions.choice: the great mountain will become a plain: every obstacle to the rebuilding will be removed
decisions.reason: The mountain stands for whatever stood in Zerubbabel's way. It may be the opposition of the peoples around, which had stopped the work for years (Ezra 4:1-5, 24; 5:3-5), or the great heap of rubble on the temple site, or the sheer size of the task. The text does not say. The picture of mountains made level is used of the LORD's coming in Isaiah 40:4.

decisions.choice: the top stone: the last stone, which marks the building complete
alternatives: the first stone, laid at the start of the building
decisions.reason: The word comes from "head", which can mean the top of something or its first or chief part. If the top stone is meant, Zerubbabel will set the last stone and so complete the temple, as verse 9 says he will finish it. Some read it as the first or chief stone, set when the work began again. The text does not describe the stone more closely.

decisions.choice: Grace, grace to it!: a shout calling down God's favor on the stone
alternatives: How beautiful, how beautiful it is!
decisions.reason: The word means favor or grace, and also charm or beauty. The people's shout may be a blessing on the finished building, asking for God's favor on it, or a cry of delight at its beauty. The first sense fits the theme of the chapter, that the work is done by God's Spirit.

decisions.choice: who do you think you are? (R); the last stone of the temple (R); God bless it! (R)
decisions.reason: Readable turns the question into a challenge, which is how it is meant, and says which stone is meant and what the shout asks for (m3). "Grace, grace" would mean little to a new reader. The closing marks end the word to Zerubbabel and the angel's words.

decisions.choice: The people's shout given after a colon without a third level of quotation marks
decisions.reason: The shout is quoted inside the LORD's word, itself inside the angel's speech; French has no settled third level of quotation marks, so the colon introduces it plainly.

decisions.choice: "¡Gracia, gracia a ella!" (L, B); "¡Que Dios la bendiga!" (R)
decisions.reason: Hen is "gracia", the key term, at L and B; R says what the shout means, as the English R does.

decisions.choice: "Neema, neema kwake!" (L, B); "Mungu alibariki!" (R)
decisions.reason: The shout calls down God's favour on the stone; "neema" is the key term for grace. Readable says what the shout asks for, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "Ân điển, ân điển cho nó!" (L, B) / "Xin Đức Chúa Trời ban phước cho nó!" (R)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision: a shout calling down God's favor; "ân điển" is the style guide's key word for grace, and Readable says what the shout asks, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: Zerubbabel is "người" in the third person, with no deity span
decisions.reason: The ruler of David's line is not God; the terms note keeps spans off the Branch and the anointed ones.

decisions.choice: "the top stone" is "머릿돌" (L), "마지막 머릿돌" (B), "성전의 마지막 돌" (R); "Grace, grace to it!" is "은총이여, 은총이여, 그것에!" (L), "은총이 있기를!" (B) and "하나님께서 복을 주시기를!" (R)
decisions.reason: The stone is the one that completes the building, not a foundation corner, so "모퉁잇돌" would mislead; the shout calls down God's favour, which Readable says plainly as the English does.

source.text: יְדֵ֣י זְרֻבָּבֶ֗ל יִסְּד֛וּ הַבַּ֥יִת הַזֶּ֖ה וְיָדָ֣יו תְּבַצַּ֑עְנָה וְיָ֣דַעְתָּ֔ כִּֽי־יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת שְׁלָחַ֥נִי אֲלֵיכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: [The] hands of Zerubbabel have founded the house this, and his hands will finish [it]; and you will know that Yahweh of hosts has sent me to you.

en.L: The hands of Zerubbabel have founded this house, and his hands will finish [it]; and you shall know that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts has sent me to you.
en.B: Zerubbabel's hands have laid the foundation of this house, and his hands will bring it to completion. Then you will know that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies has sent me to you.
en.R: Zerubbabel has laid the foundation of this temple with his own hands, and with his own hands he will finish it. Then you will know that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies has sent me to you.

fr.L: Les mains de Zorobabel ont fondé cette maison, et ses mains [l’]achèveront ; et vous saurez que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées m’a envoyé vers vous.
fr.B: Les mains de Zorobabel ont posé les fondations de cette maison, et ses mains la mèneront à son achèvement. Alors vous saurez que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées m’a envoyé vers vous.
fr.R: Zorobabel a posé les fondations de ce temple de ses propres mains, et de ses propres mains il le terminera. Alors vous saurez que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées m’a envoyé vers vous.

es.L: Las manos de Zorobabel han echado los cimientos de esta casa, y sus manos [la] terminarán; y {{plural_you:sabrán|sabréis}} que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los ejércitos me ha enviado a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.
es.B: Las manos de Zorobabel han puesto los cimientos de esta casa, y sus manos la terminarán. Entonces {{plural_you:sabrán|sabréis}} que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos me ha enviado a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.
es.R: Zorobabel ha puesto los cimientos de este templo con sus propias manos, y con sus propias manos lo terminará. Entonces {{plural_you:sabrán|sabréis}} que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos me ha enviado a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.

sw.L: Mikono ya Zerubabeli imeuweka msingi wa nyumba hii, na mikono yake itaimaliza; nanyi mtajua kwamba {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi amenituma kwenu.
sw.B: Mikono ya Zerubabeli imeuweka msingi wa nyumba hii, na mikono yake itaikamilisha. Ndipo mtajua kwamba {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi amenituma kwenu.
sw.R: Zerubabeli ameuweka msingi wa hekalu hili kwa mikono yake mwenyewe, na kwa mikono yake mwenyewe atalimaliza. Ndipo mtajua kwamba {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi amenituma kwenu.

vi.L: Tay của Xô-rô-ba-bên đã đặt nền nhà này, và tay người sẽ hoàn tất [nó]; và các ngươi sẽ biết rằng {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân đã sai tôi đến cùng các ngươi.
vi.B: Chính tay Xô-rô-ba-bên đã đặt nền nhà này, và tay người sẽ hoàn tất nó. Bấy giờ các ngươi sẽ biết rằng {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân đã sai tôi đến với các ngươi.
vi.R: Chính tay Xô-rô-ba-bên đã đặt nền đền thờ này, và chính tay người sẽ xây xong. Bấy giờ các ngươi sẽ biết rằng {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân đã sai tôi đến với các ngươi.

ko.L: 스룹바벨의 손이 이 집의 기초를 놓았으니, 그의 손이 [그것을] 마칠 것이다. 그러면 너희는 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 나를 너희에게 보내신 줄 알 것이다.
ko.B: 스룹바벨의 손이 이 집의 기초를 놓았으니, 그의 손이 그것을 완성할 것이다. 그때에 너희는 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 나를 너희에게 보내신 줄 알게 될 것이다.
ko.R: 스룹바벨이 자기 손으로 이 성전의 기초를 놓았으니, 자기 손으로 그것을 완성할 것이다. 그때에 너희는 하늘의 군대를 거느리신 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 나를 너희에게 보내신 줄 알게 될 것이다.

decisions.choice: founded this house: began building the temple
decisions.reason: Ezra 3:8-10 tells of the foundation laid under Zerubbabel and Jeshua soon after the return, and Haggai 2:18 dates the founding of the temple to the year of this prophecy, 520 BC, when the stalled work began again. The verb can mean the start of the building as a whole. The temple was finished in the sixth year of Darius, 515 BC (Ezra 6:14-15).

decisions.choice: you will know that the LORD of hosts has sent me: the finished temple will prove the message true
decisions.reason: The words are the same as in 2:13 and 2:15. When Zerubbabel completes the temple, the people will know that the prophet spoke for the LORD (Deuteronomy 18:21-22). "You" is singular here, perhaps speaking to Zechariah, perhaps to each hearer.

decisions.choice: temple (R); with his own hands (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says "temple" for "house" and makes the point of "his hands" plain: the man who began the work will finish it himself. Literal says "you shall know", as in 2:13 and 2:15.

source.text: כִּ֣י מִ֣י בַז֮ לְי֣וֹם קְטַנּוֹת֒ וְשָׂמְח֗וּ וְרָא֞וּ אֶת־הָאֶ֧בֶן הַבְּדִ֛יל בְּיַ֥ד זְרֻבָּבֶ֖ל שִׁבְעָה־אֵ֑לֶּה עֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה הֵ֥מָּה מְשׁוֹטְטִ֖ים בְּכָל־הָאָֽרֶץ׃

records.literal_gloss: For who has despised [the] day of small things? And they will rejoice and see the stone the tin in [the] hand of Zerubbabel. These seven [are] the eyes of Yahweh; they range in all the earth.

en.L: For who has despised the day of small things? They will rejoice and see the tin stone in the hand of Zerubbabel. These seven [are] the eyes of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; they range through all the earth.
en.B: Who has despised the day of small beginnings? People will rejoice when they see the plumb stone in Zerubbabel's hand. These seven are the eyes of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, which range over the whole earth.
en.R: Some people looked down on the work because it began so small. But they will be glad when they see Zerubbabel holding the plumb stone. These seven lamps are the eyes of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, which look over the whole earth.

fr.L: Car qui a méprisé le jour des petites choses ? Ils se réjouiront et verront la pierre d’étain dans la main de Zorobabel. Ces sept-là [sont] les yeux {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} ; ils parcourent toute la terre.
fr.B: Qui a méprisé le jour des humbles commencements ? On se réjouira en voyant le fil à plomb dans la main de Zorobabel. Ces sept lampes sont les yeux {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, qui parcourent toute la terre.
fr.R: Certains ont méprisé le travail parce qu’il avait commencé si petit. Mais ils seront heureux quand ils verront Zorobabel tenir le fil à plomb. Ces sept lampes sont les yeux {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, qui surveillent toute la terre.

es.L: Porque ¿quién ha despreciado el día de las cosas pequeñas? Se alegrarán y verán la piedra de estaño en la mano de Zorobabel. Estos siete [son] los ojos {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}; recorren toda la tierra.
es.B: ¿Quién ha despreciado el día de los comienzos pequeños? La gente se alegrará cuando vea la plomada en la mano de Zorobabel. Estos siete son los ojos {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, que recorren toda la tierra.
es.R: Algunos despreciaron la obra porque comenzó tan pequeña. Pero se alegrarán cuando vean a Zorobabel con la plomada en la mano. Estas siete lámparas son los ojos {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, que vigilan toda la tierra.

sw.L: Kwa maana ni nani aliyeidharau siku ya mambo madogo? Watafurahi na kuliona jiwe la bati mkononi mwa Zerubabeli. Hizi saba [ni] macho ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}; yanazunguka katika dunia yote.
sw.B: Ni nani aliyeidharau siku ya mwanzo mdogo? Watu watafurahi watakapoliona jiwe la timazi mkononi mwa Zerubabeli. Hizi saba ni macho ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, yanayozunguka dunia yote.
sw.R: Watu wengine waliidharau kazi hii kwa sababu ilianza kidogo sana. Lakini watafurahi watakapomwona Zerubabeli ameshika jiwe la timazi. Taa hizi saba ni macho ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, yanayotazama dunia yote.

vi.L: Vì ai đã khinh dể ngày của những việc nhỏ? Họ sẽ vui mừng và thấy hòn đá thiếc trong tay Xô-rô-ba-bên. Bảy [ngọn đèn] này [là] mắt của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}; chúng đi khắp cả đất.
vi.B: Ai đã dám khinh thường ngày của những khởi đầu nhỏ bé? Người ta sẽ vui mừng khi thấy quả dọi trong tay Xô-rô-ba-bên. Bảy ngọn đèn này là mắt của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, nhìn khắp cả đất.
vi.R: Có người đã coi thường công việc này vì nó bắt đầu quá nhỏ bé. Nhưng họ sẽ vui mừng khi thấy Xô-rô-ba-bên cầm quả dọi trong tay. Bảy ngọn đèn này là mắt của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, nhìn xem khắp cả đất.

ko.L: 작은 일들의 날을 누가 업신여겼느냐? 그들이 스룹바벨의 손에 있는 주석 돌을 보고 기뻐할 것이다. 이 일곱은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 눈이니, 온 땅을 두루 살핀다.
ko.B: 작은 시작의 날을 누가 업신여기느냐? 사람들이 스룹바벨의 손에 들린 다림추를 보고 기뻐할 것이다. 이 일곱은 온 땅을 두루 살피는 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 눈이다.
ko.R: 어떤 사람들은 일이 아주 작게 시작되었다고 업신여겼다. 그러나 그들은 스룹바벨이 다림추를 들고 있는 것을 보면 기뻐할 것이다. 이 일곱 등잔은 온 세상을 두루 살피시는 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 눈이다.

decisions.choice: the day of small things: a time of small beginnings
decisions.reason: The new temple seemed nothing compared with Solomon's (Haggai 2:3), and older people who had seen the first temple wept when its foundation was laid (Ezra 3:12). The question rebukes those who looked down on the work because it was small.

decisions.choice: they will rejoice: those who despised the small beginnings will rejoice when they see the work going on
alternatives: these seven, the eyes of the LORD, will rejoice when they see the stone in Zerubbabel's hand
decisions.reason: The Hebrew can be divided in two ways. The verbs "rejoice" and "see" may have as their subject the people who despised the work: they will change their minds. Or "these seven" may be the subject: the LORD's eyes will see the work with joy. The main division of the Hebrew falls after "Zerubbabel", which favors the first reading.

decisions.choice: the tin stone: a builder's plumb weight
alternatives: an inscribed tin or lead tablet for the foundation
decisions.reason: The second word usually means tin (Numbers 31:22; Ezekiel 22:18), so the phrase is "the stone, the tin". It is most often read as a plumb weight of tin or lead hanging from a line, used to check that a wall is straight. Zerubbabel holding it means that he is in charge of the building. The same letters can mean "separation" or "chosen", and some read a stone set apart for the building, or a metal tablet laid in the foundation.

decisions.choice: these seven are the eyes of the LORD: the seven lamps show God's watchful care over all the earth
decisions.reason: "These seven" are the seven lamps of verse 2. The angel explains them as the LORD's eyes, which see everything. 2 Chronicles 16:9 says the same: "the eyes of the LORD range throughout the whole earth to strengthen those whose heart is true to him". The seven eyes on the stone in 3:9 seem to be the same.

decisions.choice: Some people looked down on the work because it began so small (R); These seven lamps (R)
decisions.reason: Readable turns the question into a plain statement of what it means and says "lamps", since "these seven" points back to the seven lamps. Balanced says "plumb stone" for the tin stone (m3), and Literal keeps the Hebrew word.

decisions.choice: "la pierre d'étain" (L); "le fil à plomb" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The English Literal keeps "tin stone" and the other levels say "plumb stone"; French says "fil à plomb", as Amos 7:7-8, since "pierre de plomb" is not a French tool name.

decisions.choice: "la piedra de estaño" (L); "la plomada" (B, R)
decisions.reason: L keeps the Hebrew "tin stone"; B and R say "plomada", the builder's weight, the word used for 'anakh in Amos 7:7-8 in Spanish.

decisions.choice: "jiwe la bati" (L); "jiwe la timazi" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew "tin stone"; Balanced and Readable name it as the builder's plumb weight, with "timazi" as in 2 Kings 21:13 and Amos 7:7.

decisions.choice: "hòn đá thiếc" (L) / "quả dọi" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision: a builder's plumb weight; Literal keeps "tin stone", Balanced and Readable name the tool, the weight of Amos 7:7's "dây dọi".

decisions.choice: "Bảy [ngọn đèn] này" at Literal
decisions.reason: Vietnamese needs a noun after "bảy"; the meaning decision says the seven are the lamps.

decisions.choice: "the tin stone" is "주석 돌" (L) and "다림추" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew words; Balanced and Readable name the builder's plumb weight, as the English "plumb stone" does (footnoted in the meaning decision). It is kept apart from Amos's "다림줄" (plumb line), which is a different word.

decisions.choice: Readable gives the LORD's eyes the honorific ("살피시는"); Literal and Balanced keep the plain verb with "눈" as subject
decisions.reason: The angel speaks of God here, so -시- is fitting; at Literal and Balanced the eyes themselves are the subject, and Korean does not put -시- on a body part without the person.

source.text: וָאַ֖עַן וָאֹמַ֣ר אֵלָ֑יו מַה־שְּׁנֵ֤י הַזֵּיתִים֙ הָאֵ֔לֶה עַל־יְמִ֥ין הַמְּנוֹרָ֖ה וְעַל־שְׂמֹאולָֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And I answered and said to him, What [are] the two olive trees the these on the right of the lampstand and on its left?

en.L: And I answered and said to him, "What [are] these two olive trees on the right of the lampstand and on its left?"
en.B: Then I asked him, "What are these two olive trees to the right and left of the lampstand?"
en.R: Then I asked the angel, "What are these two olive trees, one on the right side of the lampstand and one on the left?"

fr.L: Et je pris la parole et lui dis : « Que [sont] ces deux oliviers à la droite du chandelier et à sa gauche ? »
fr.B: Puis je lui demandai : « Que sont ces deux oliviers à droite et à gauche du chandelier ? »
fr.R: Puis j’ai demandé à l’ange : « Que sont ces deux oliviers, l’un à droite du chandelier et l’autre à gauche ? »

es.L: Y respondí y le dije: «¿Qué [son] estos dos olivos a la derecha del candelabro y a su izquierda?».
es.B: Entonces le pregunté: «¿Qué son estos dos olivos a la derecha y a la izquierda del candelabro?».
es.R: Entonces le pregunté al ángel: «¿Qué son estos dos olivos, uno al lado derecho del candelabro y otro al izquierdo?».

sw.L: Nami nikajibu, nikamwambia, "Mizeituni hii miwili iliyo upande wa kuume wa kinara na upande wake wa kushoto [ni] nini?"
sw.B: Kisha nikamwuliza, "Mizeituni hii miwili iliyo upande wa kuume na wa kushoto wa kinara ni nini?"
sw.R: Kisha nikamwuliza malaika, "Mizeituni hii miwili, mmoja upande wa kulia wa kinara na mwingine upande wa kushoto, ni nini?"

vi.L: Tôi đáp lời và nói với người: "Hai cây ô-liu này ở bên phải chân đèn và bên trái nó [là] gì?"
vi.B: Bấy giờ tôi hỏi người: "Hai cây ô-liu ở bên phải và bên trái chân đèn này là gì?"
vi.R: Bấy giờ tôi hỏi thiên sứ: "Hai cây ô-liu này, một cây ở bên phải chân đèn và một cây ở bên trái, là gì vậy?"

ko.L: 그리고 내가 대답하여 그에게 말했다. "등잔대의 오른쪽과 왼쪽에 있는 이 올리브나무 두 그루는 무엇입니까?"
ko.B: 내가 그에게 물었다. "등잔대 오른쪽과 왼쪽에 있는 이 올리브나무 두 그루는 무엇입니까?"
ko.R: 내가 천사에게 물었다. "등잔대 오른쪽에 하나, 왼쪽에 하나 있는 이 올리브나무 두 그루는 무엇입니까?"

decisions.choice: Zechariah asks again: the vision resumes
decisions.reason: The angel has explained the seven lamps, but not the trees. Zechariah asks about them twice (verses 11 and 12), the second time more precisely.

decisions.choice: the angel (R)
decisions.reason: Readable names the angel for "him", since the word to Zerubbabel has come between.

source.text: וָאַ֣עַן שֵׁנִ֔ית וָאֹמַ֖ר אֵלָ֑יו מַה־שְׁתֵּ֞י שִׁבֲּלֵ֣י הַזֵּיתִ֗ים אֲשֶׁר֙ בְּיַ֗ד שְׁנֵי֙ צַנְתְּר֣וֹת הַזָּהָ֔ב הַֽמְרִיקִ֥ים מֵעֲלֵיהֶ֖ם הַזָּהָֽב׃

records.literal_gloss: And I answered a second [time] and said to him, What [are the] two branches of the olive trees which [are] beside [the] two pipes of the gold, which empty out from them the gold?

en.L: And I answered a second time and said to him, "What [are] the two branches of the olive trees that [are] beside the two golden pipes, which pour out from themselves the gold?"
en.B: I asked him again, "What are the two branches of the olive trees beside the two gold pipes that pour out the golden oil?"
en.R: I asked him again, "What are the two olive branches beside the two gold pipes? Golden oil is pouring out through them."

fr.L: Et je pris la parole une seconde fois et lui dis : « Que [sont] les deux rameaux des oliviers qui [sont] à côté des deux conduits d’or, qui déversent d’eux-mêmes l’or ? »
fr.B: Je lui demandai encore : « Que sont les deux rameaux d’olivier à côté des deux conduits d’or qui déversent l’huile dorée ? »
fr.R: Je lui ai encore demandé : « Que sont les deux branches d’olivier à côté des deux conduits en or ? De l’huile dorée coule par ces conduits. »

es.L: Y respondí por segunda vez y le dije: «¿Qué [son] las dos ramas de los olivos que [están] junto a los dos conductos de oro, que vierten de sí el oro?».
es.B: Le pregunté otra vez: «¿Qué son las dos ramas de olivo que están junto a los dos conductos de oro que vierten el aceite dorado?».
es.R: Le pregunté otra vez: «¿Qué son las dos ramas de olivo que están junto a los dos conductos de oro? Por ellos sale aceite dorado».

sw.L: Nami nikajibu mara ya pili, nikamwambia, "Matawi mawili ya mizeituni yaliyo kando ya mirija miwili ya dhahabu, inayomimina dhahabu kutoka ndani yake, [ni] nini?"
sw.B: Nikamwuliza tena, "Matawi mawili ya mizeituni yaliyo kando ya mirija miwili ya dhahabu inayomimina mafuta ya dhahabu ni nini?"
sw.R: Nikamwuliza tena, "Matawi haya mawili ya mizeituni yaliyo kando ya mirija miwili ya dhahabu ni nini? Mafuta ya dhahabu yanamiminika kupitia mirija hiyo."

vi.L: Tôi đáp lời lần thứ hai và nói với người: "Hai nhánh của các cây ô-liu [ở] bên cạnh hai ống bằng vàng, là những ống đổ vàng ra từ chính chúng, [là] gì?"

decisions.choice: branches: olive branches heavy with fruit

decisions.choice: pipes: channels carrying oil from the trees to the lampstand

decisions.choice: the gold: the golden oil

decisions.choice: the two sons of fresh oil: two people set apart by anointing
alternatives: two who are full of oil
decisions.reason: "Son of" a thing means one who belongs to it or is marked by it. Kings and priests were anointed with oil when they took office (Exodus 29:7; 1 Samuel 16:13), so "sons of oil" are most likely two anointed leaders. The word here is the one for fresh oil, not the usual word for anointing oil, so some read "the two who supply oil". The angel does not name them. In the book's setting they are most often taken as Joshua the high priest and Zerubbabel, the heir of David, the two leaders named in chapters 3 and 4; together they serve the LORD as his chosen leaders.

decisions.choice: the Lord of all the earth: God as ruler of the whole world
decisions.reason: The title is used of God in Joshua 3:11, 13, Micah 4:13 and Psalm 97:5. It fits the visions, in which the LORD's eyes and riders go through all the earth.

decisions.choice: Revelation 11:4: the two witnesses are "the two olive trees and the two lampstands"
decisions.reason: Revelation takes up this vision for the two witnesses who prophesy in the last days and stand "before the Lord of the earth".
